title: Runtime affinity oscillation remediation plan and follow-up
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-28 capacity window we observed a sustained throughput regression and p95/p99 token latency increase for several hosted clusters running quantized Llama-family variants. Investigation showed the new dynamic kernel affinity scoring (deployed 2026-02-20) causes oscillation in kernel selection when combined with varying batch sizes and our KV cache warmup heuristics. This ticket tracks the remediation work: short-term mitigations, medium-term fixes to the scheduler scoring algorithm, and long-term hardening (tests, telemetry, runbooks).
postmortem_summary:
Timeline of events:
- 2026-02-20: kernel-affinity v2 scoring rolled to prod behind feature flag FF-KAF2 (canary 10%).
- 2026-02-25: FF-KAF2 promoted to 70% to meet throughput targets.
- 2026-02-28 02:14 UTC: alerts triggered for increased p99 token latency across multi-tenant pool eu-west-1-g4.
- 2026-02-28 02:30 UTC: oncall reverted promotion to 10% (partial rollback).
- 2026-02-28 03:45 UTC: mitigations (forcing deterministic tie-break) reduced oscillation but did not restore baseline.
Root cause (summary): kernel scoring prioritized kernel A for short sequences and kernel B for longer sequences based on recent latency samples; when batch-size variance was high the scoring loop reacted to transient samples and flipped affinity rapidly, causing cache misses, attention fallback into slower path, and increased tail latency. The scheduler lacked hysteresis and a deterministic tie-break for equivalent scores, which amplified oscillation.
impact_details: Impacted services: hosted API (text generation), dedicated pools with mixed-model tenants. Customer visible symptoms: slowed completion times for streaming responses, increased error budget consumption for several enterprise customers. Internal metrics: 30% increase in p99 token latency on affected pools, 12% drop in throughput for quantized-16 kernels during the window.
short_term_mitigations:
1) Immediately re-enable the previous stable kernel scoring (rollback to v1) for all clusters while remediation is developed (completed 2026-02-28).
2) Add deterministic tie-break based on kernel ID and node-stable hash to scheduler to stop flip-flopping (partial: feature flag FF-KAF2-TIE enabled 2026-03-02).
3) Temporarily clamp scoring sensitivity by increasing the smoothing factor (alpha) to reduce reaction to single-sample spikes (deployed 2026-03-03 to affected zones).
long_term_plan:
1) Implement hysteresis and minimum dwell time for kernel affinity decisions so an affinity must hold for N requests or T ms before switching.
2) Replace the simple exponential smoothing with a quantile-aware estimator that tracks p50/p95/p99 separately and weights decisions towards p95 stability.
3) Add a mode-aware scoring path that factors in sequence-length histogram and batch-size distribution for each route.
4) Integrate kernel selection A/B experiments into the CI benchmark harness so changes are validated against representative traffic traces before release.
action_items: A1: Revert non-essential scoring heuristics from v2 until hysteresis is in place — owner: Miguel Torres — due: 2026-03-05 — status: done
A2: Implement deterministic tie-break and publish design doc — owner: Priya Singh — due: 2026-03-08 — status: in progress
A3: Add dwell-time policy (configurable) into scheduler and expose in runtime config — owner: Daniel Kim — due: 2026-03-15 — status: in progress
A4: Extend telemetry: add kernel-selection event stream and per-request kernel decision tag (sampling 100%) — owner: DataInfra (team) / contact: Lara Chen — due: 2026-03-12 — status: in progress
A5: Create a microbenchmark that replays real client batch-size distributions and sequence lengths and validate kernel-selection stability — owner: SRE Bench — due: 2026-03-18 — status: planned
A6: Postmortem review and customer communication draft for affected enterprise accounts — owner: Natasha Ivanov — due: 2026-03-10 — status: done
A7: Add automated regression test to release gate measuring p95 token latency on quantized variants — owner: CI Team — due: 2026-03-22 — status: planned
A8: Prepare canary rollout plan with traffic shadowing for runtime-1.25 — owner: Release Eng — due: 2026-03-20 — status: planned
acceptance_criteria:
- Affinity oscillations reduced to baseline: per-pool kernel-change-rate <= 2 changes/min under representative traffic.
- p95/p99 token latency measured on replay harness within 5% of pre-regression baseline for quantized-16 models.
- New telemetry surfaces kernel-decisions and provides an alert when change-rate exceeds threshold.
- All changes behind feature flag with documented canary plan and automated rollback hooks.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for tie-break and dwell-time logic.
- Integration: scheduler + runtime integration test running with synthetic batch distributions.
- Replay harness: run nightly against 7-day traffic sample; baseline comparisons stored per-run.
- Canary: rollout to 5% traffic with shadowing, monitor kernel-change-rate and p95 for 48h before promotion.
comments: 2026-03-01 Miguel Torres: Initial triage — identified correlation between scoring updates and increased kernel-change-rate. Placed rollback on critical clusters.
2026-03-02 Priya Singh: Prototype tie-break implemented. Observed immediate reduction in flip-flop on unit harness (local). Needs integration tests.
2026-03-03 Lara Chen: Telemetry schema v2 submitted. Will add kernel_decision, kernel_score, batch_size, seq_len to event payload. Sampling set to 100% for first 48h after rollout in canary.
2026-03-04 Daniel Kim: Suggested dwell-time default 1000ms / 3 requests based on simulation. Trade-off: slightly slower adaptation to real regressions but large reduction in thrash.
2026-03-06 Natasha Ivanov: Customer comms drafted and approved by PM; legal reviewed wording for enterprise SLAs.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Trade-off: adding dwell-time increases time to adapt to a genuine performance regression on a kernel; mitigated by making dwell-time configurable and adding a fast-path for explicit operator override.
- Trade-off: more telemetry increases cost and storage; mitigation is short-lived 100% sampling during canary followed by adaptive sampling.
- We're prioritizing stability (reduce oscillation) over micro-optimizations for throughput in short term to restore SLAs.
next_steps:
1) Finish and merge tie-break PR, run full integration tests (owner: Priya).
2) Deploy dwell-time config to staging and run replay harness (owner: Daniel/SRE Bench).
3) Wire alerts for kernel-change-rate and include in oncall runbook (owner: SRE).
4) Schedule cross-team postmortem review with API, SRE, Release Eng and PM (owner: Asha).

- 2026-03-02: feature flag FF-KAF2-TIE toggled in canary zones.
- 2026-03-03: smoothing factor increased (alpha=0.2) in prod for effected clusters.
- 2026-03-06: customer comms sent to 3 enterprise customers.
